Analyzing mathematica AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the PKGBUILD is sourced, executing its global/top-level code. The key concern is the conditional block that fetches a dynamic download signature:

```bash
if [[ ${SKIP_DYNAMIC_SIGNATURE:-${PRINTSRCINFO}} != 1 ]]; then
  _dynamic_signature=$(
    set -o pipefail
    curl -fsSL https://www.wolfram.com/download-center/ \
      | grep -oP "\bhref=\"${_source_url/./\.}\?[^\"]+\K&signature=[a-zA-Z0-9]+(?=\"|&)" \
      | uniq
  )
fi
```

During `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, `PRINTSRCINFO=1` is set, so the condition evaluates to false and the curl does NOT run. During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, `PRINTSRCINFO` is unset, so the curl WILL execute. However, this curl downloads the public HTML page from `wolfram.com` (the project's own upstream), extracts a signature parameter via `grep -oP`, and uses it to construct the installer download URL. This is documented standard practice for the Mathematica package, which requires a dynamic signature parameter for downloads. No data is exfiltrated, no downloaded code is executed, and the destination is the package's own vendor. The rest of the top-level code consists of standard variable assignments and an `IFS` read for version parsing. `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` are not executed under `--nobuild --noprepare`.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Top-level code only fetches signature from wolfram.com; standard packaging practice.</summary>
</security_assessment>
